newsitem.title: USA: U.S. denies NATO trying to squeeze Russia out.
newsitem.headline: U.S. denies NATO trying to squeeze Russia out.

text.p: Secretary of State Madeleine Albright denied on Thursday that the United States or its NATO allies were trying to squeeze Russia out of Europe by expanding the alliance to include ex-communist states.

The United States is leading the alliance campaign for expansion, which faces a crucial moment at a July NATO summit in Madrid when the first post-Cold War invitations to ex-communist states are to be issued.
Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are the top contenders, but Romania and Slovenia are under discussion.
Albright noted as part of the enlargement effort NATO was negotiating with Russia a sweetner package designed to calm fears about expansion.
"Nobody's trying to squeeze them (Russia) out of Europe," Albright said in an interview on the PBS programme "Newshour with Jim Lehrer."
"They will have a voice ... they will be part of consultations," she said.
Albright acknowledged that the Russians disapproved of NATO enlargement but said Moscow knew it would go forward on schedule.

"There is no one enemy that NATO is directed at. It is the strongest alliance of democracies ever, and these countries want to be in it, and Russia is not to be excluded from Europe and will also have an ongoing relationship with the United States," Albright said.

Russian President Boris Yeltsin, in his annual state of the nation address on Thursday, attacked NATO's plans, calling them an attempt to "squeeze" Russia out of Europe and warned the continent would pay a heavy price.

"We are against NATO's plans for eastward expansion. Their realisation will deliver a direct blow to our security. Behind them is the aspiration to squeeze Russia out of Europe and to leave it politically isolated," Yeltsin said.
Albright said the Russia-NATO charter under discussion would define Moscow's ties with the alliance and ensure a permanent mechanism for regular dialogue and cooperation.

Albright discussed the package in Moscow with Yeltsin two weeks ago and Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbott was holding more talks in Moscow this week. Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov will visit Washington at the weekend for further meetings.
U.S. officials hope there will be concrete progress on the thorny issue at the summit on March 19 and 20 in Helsinki between Clinton and Yeltsin.
